sources.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017–2018 (DEMO_J, BMX_J)
sources.publisher: CDC / National Center for Health Statistics
sources.population: Nationally representative sample of the U.S. civilian non-institutionalized population. Benchmarks use participants aged 20–24 examined in the Mobile Examination Center.
sources.statisticalMethod: Survey-weighted empirical cumulative distribution using the 2-year MEC exam weight (WTMEC2YR). Uncertainty is a 95% Wilson interval at the Kish effective sample size.
limitations: A single 2-year cycle: each age/sex group holds only a few hundred participants, so the extreme tails are imprecise.
The intervals use the Kish effective sample size and ignore NHANES clustering and stratification, so true design-based intervals are wider.
Data were collected in 2017–2018 and population values may have shifted since.
Comparisons are with U.S. adults of your age band, not with athletes or students specifically.
sources.license: Public domain (U.S. federal government data). NCHS data-use restrictions apply: the data may not be used to identify any individual.

retrieval.notes: cdc.gov was blocked by the network policy of the build environment (2026-10-26), so byte-for-byte copies of the CDC release files were taken from public GitHub mirrors: DEMO_J/BMX_J from github.com/Pranav-error/fatty_liver_pilot, DEMO_H/BPX_H/SLQ_H from github.com/balr411/biostat625FinalProject. Each file's record count matches the CDC data documentation, its SAS creation timestamp matches the CDC release, and the build cross-checked it against pandas.read_sas. SHA-256 hashes are listed so anyone can compare them with files downloaded from cdc.gov (npm run benchmarks:fetch && npm run benchmarks:build).

sources.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013–2014 (DEMO_H, BPX_H, SLQ_H)
sources.publisher: CDC / National Center for Health Statistics
sources.population: Nationally representative sample of the U.S. civilian non-institutionalized population. Benchmarks use participants aged 20–24.
sources.statisticalMethod: Survey-weighted empirical cumulative distribution: MEC exam weight (WTMEC2YR) for examination measures, interview weight (WTINT2YR) for questionnaire items. Uncertainty is a 95% Wilson interval at the Kish effective sample size.
limitations: A single 2-year cycle: each age/sex group holds only a few hundred participants, so the extreme tails are imprecise.
The intervals use the Kish effective sample size and ignore NHANES clustering and stratification, so true design-based intervals are wider.
Data were collected in 2013–2014 and population values may have shifted since.
Comparisons are with U.S. adults of your age band, not with athletes or students specifically.
sources.license: Public domain (U.S. federal government data). NCHS data-use restrictions apply: the data may not be used to identify any individual.

retrieval.notes: cdc.gov was blocked by the network policy of the build environment (2026-10-26), so byte-for-byte copies of the CDC release files were taken from public GitHub mirrors: DEMO_J/BMX_J from github.com/Pranav-error/fatty_liver_pilot, DEMO_H/BPX_H/SLQ_H from github.com/balr411/biostat625FinalProject. Each file's record count matches the CDC data documentation, its SAS creation timestamp matches the CDC release, and the build cross-checked it against pandas.read_sas. SHA-256 hashes are listed so anyone can compare them with files downloaded from cdc.gov (npm run benchmarks:fetch && npm run benchmarks:build).
